text: Agile methodology helps teams build software in a flexible, iterative way. Work is divided into short cycles called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Before each sprint, the team chooses user stories from the backlog, a prioritized list of tasks and features. During daily standups, members share progress and discuss problems. Instead of planning everything at once, agile teams use iterative development: they build, test, and improve the product step by step. This approach allows quick feedback and makes it easier to adapt when requirements change. As a result, teams can deliver useful software sooner and keep customers happier.
